column1: # Foreign keys from a tenant-scoped table into a tenant-scoped table that do not
# name the tenant column, and are not failing the build today.
# Read by tools/checks/tenant_scoped_references.py and by
# TenantScopedReferenceCatalogTests, which derives the same set from
# `pg_constraint` on a migrated database. Both refuse an entry with no reason and
# both refuse an entry for a reference that no longer exists, so this file cannot
# drift from the schema in either direction.
# Format: reference <TAB> verdict <TAB> reason
#   reference  schema.table.constraint_name, exactly as PostgreSQL names it
#   verdict    one of the three below
#   reason     why this one is not simply fixed. A name with no reason is what
#              let twenty-three of these become invisible; the loader rejects it.
# Verdicts:
#   TENANT_FREE_TARGET      the referenced table holds no tenant-owned rows at
#                           all. This is not a tenant-blind reference, it is a
#                           tenant-free one, and nothing is wrong with it.
#   MIXED_OWNERSHIP_TARGET  the referenced table's tenant_id is nullable by
#                           design: it holds platform-owned rows (tenant_id NULL)
#                           beside tenant-owned ones. A foreign key on the RAW
#                           columns cannot express "this tenant's row or the
#                           platform's" — under MATCH SIMPLE a NULL anywhere in
#                           the key stops the check entirely, so the platform case
#                           would become unchecked while the cross-tenant case
#                           stayed possible.
#                           That is a fact about the raw columns and not about
#                           databases. V0088 closes four of these with a key on
#                           DERIVED ones: coalesce(tenant_id, nil) on the target
#                           makes the platform's ownership a value rather than an
#                           absence, and on the referencing side a declared
#                           ownership boolean generates a key column that can hold
#                           only the platform sentinel or the row's own tenant.
#                           V0086 closes the fifth with a pair of triggers, for the
#                           reason its entry gives.
#                           An entry here is therefore a SHAPE and not necessarily
#                           an open hole: the constraint sweep asks whether a key
#                           names a column spelled tenant_id, and neither a derived
#                           owner column nor a trigger is spelled that way. Every
#                           entry has to say which it is, and where the guarantee
#                           lives if it is not in the key.
#   DEFERRED                fixable exactly as V0077 fixed fourteen others, and
#                           deferred for a stated reason with the work named.
# The list may only shrink.
# MIXED_OWNERSHIP_TARGET — the five a key on the raw columns cannot fix
# DEFERRED — fixable as V0077 fixed the others, deferred for a stated reason
